cards.text: Friend, meet Zechariah, a prophet. Earlier, God gave him a message for the people: "Return to Me" (Zechariah 1:3). Now it's a few months later, in the second year of Darius, king of Persia (Ezra 4:24), and the word of the LORD comes to Zechariah again.

Zechariah looks out into the night and sees a man riding a red horse among the myrtle trees in the hollow, with red, sorrel and white horses behind him. Friend, I can't find a light switch at night, and this man is calling out horse colors.

cards.question: Zechariah is looking at a man on a red horse and a group of horses in the middle of the night. What does he do?

answers.text: He runs to tell the people

cards.text: Zechariah asks, "What are these, my lord?" An angel who is speaking with him replies, "I will show you what they are."

cards.question: Then the man among the myrtle trees explains the horses. He says the LORD sent them to ___ the earth.

cards.text: Then the riders answer the angel of the LORD, who is standing among the myrtle trees. They've patrolled the earth, and the report is IN.

cards.question: The riders have patrolled the earth. They report that all the earth is at ___ and tranquil.

cards.text: At rest and tranquil. The whole world just hit the snooze button.

cards.question: Then the angel of the LORD speaks to the LORD of Hosts. What does he ask?

answers.text: How long He will withhold mercy from Jerusalem
Why the whole earth is at rest right now
Where the riders should be sent out next

cards.question: The angel of the LORD says God has been angry with Jerusalem and the cities of Judah for seventy years.

cards.text: "How long." Friend, I asked that so many times in the junk drawer, the dead batteries I shared it with started answering for me. "A WHILE, Dorin. It's gonna be a while."

cards.question: The LORD speaks harsh and angry words to the angel who is speaking with Zechariah.

cards.text: Kind and comforting words. Hold on to that, friend, because Zechariah's about to get a message to proclaim.
The angel who is speaking with Zechariah tells him, "Proclaim this word." And it's straight from the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The first thing the LORD of Hosts says is about Jerusalem and Zion. How does He say He feels about them?

cards.text: Very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion. To me, that sounds like a God who never stopped caring, and then He talks about the nations that are at ease.

cards.question: The LORD says He is fiercely angry with the nations that are at ease.
The LORD says He was only a little angry with His people. What did the nations do?

cards.text: You ever drop ONE cookie box, and some guy walking by knocks the whole stack down too? The nations piled on, so the LORD says, therefore, here's what's coming.

cards.question: The LORD says He will return to Jerusalem. How will He return?
The LORD says that in Jerusalem, His ___ will be rebuilt.

cards.text: And a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem. I love a measuring line, friend, because I measure dough by eyeballing it, and my cookies come out in three sizes: small, medium and "what HAPPENED here."

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts also says His cities will again overflow with prosperity.
The LORD says He will again comfort Zion. What does He say He will do with Jerusalem?

cards.text: Overflow. Comfort. Choose. That's the word "again" twice in one breath, friend, and I'll take an "again" any day.
Then Zechariah looks up and sees four horns. Just four horns, so he asks the angel who is speaking with him, "What are these?"

cards.question: The angel explains the four horns. What did these horns do to Judah, Israel and Jerusalem?

cards.text: Then the LORD shows Zechariah four craftsmen. Four horns that scattered His people, and here comes the WORK CREW.

cards.question: Zechariah asks what the craftsmen are coming to do. They've come to ___ the horns and throw them ___.
The horns had scattered Judah so that no one could raise his head.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Zechariah for now. Trust me, friend, this prophet's still got more to see.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has 7 story cards and only 6 choice cards.

rule.text: Choice cards are equal to or more than story cards in every stop.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "Proclaim this word.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke 'this man is calling out horse colors' comes right after 'a man riding a red horse,' so it reads as if the rider is calling out colors. It is Zechariah who sees and names the horses. The image doesn't click without working it out.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The question keeps 'and tranquil' next to the blank. That makes 'war' and 'risk' impossible fits, so 'rest' stands out as the only answer that works.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answer to card 7 ('At rest and tranquil') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card is only a joke on the words 'How long' from 1:12, which cards 9 and 10 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card runs to four sentences: "How long." / the drawer line / "A WHILE, Dorin." / "It's gonna be a while."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card restates the answers from cards 10 and 11 ('Overflow. Comfort. Choose.') and tells nothing new from the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card runs to four sentences: 'Overflow.' 'Comfort.' 'Choose.' plus the closing line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Just four horns, so he asks' gives a reason for Zechariah's question that the text never gives. The text says only that he looked up, saw four horns and asked (Zech 1:18-19). 'Just' also suggests he saw nothing else, which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'back' for the second blank is close to 'down.' A baker could argue that 'throw them back' (drive the horns back) fits what the craftsmen do.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: No card says that the horns are 'the horns of the nations that have lifted up their horns against the land of Judah' (Zech 1:21). That is the vision's own explanation of what the horns are, and it is an important detail. The cards only ever say 'the horns.'

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The line that says the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.'). Only a few words are changed.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
